reuse.why: Extracts the repeated category query into getVisibleCategoriesWithoutTemplates and uses it for five actions, but copyPreviousMonth keeps its own rule, the #fixed tag is matched with SQL LIKE instead of the existing extractTagsFromText, and the new action re-writes the income/sign handling.

duplication.why: The hidden/template/#fixed exclusion is written twice (WHERE clause of the new helper and CASE columns plus an inline condition for copyPreviousMonth), and setLastMonthSpending repeats the per-action income-tracking check and sign inversion.

placement.why: Selection lives in actions.ts as a shared query helper next to getBudgetData and the handler is registered in budget/app.ts; the rule being split between SQL and TypeScript blurs where it is decided.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps, though it also removes an income-category fixture from the unrelated copyUntilYearEnd test setup.

maintainability.why: The helper name getVisibleCategoriesWithoutTemplates no longer describes what it does (it can include hidden and excludes #fixed), the rule exists in two SQL forms, and the substring LIKE '%#fixed%' matches other tags.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth decides the exclusions from getBudgetData's CASE columns instead of the shared category selection; #fixed detection uses LIKE instead of shared/tags extractTagsFromText.

disguised_duplication.where: getBudgetData's has_template/is_fixed CASE columns plus copyPreviousMonth's condition reshape the WHERE filter of getVisibleCategoriesWithoutTemplates into computed flags.

abstraction_drift.where: getVisibleCategoriesWithoutTemplates gains includeHiddenCategories and the #fixed filter while keeping a name that says neither; copyPreviousMonth re-implements the same exclusion via getBudgetData instead of calling it.
